items.title: Correct three inherited chemical-property blocks that contradict the stated substance form
items.body:
# Correct three inherited chemical-property blocks that contradict the stated substance form

Reviewed W02 head `0597d00417be4d7cdfb5a31970043eec9bbc88fe`, frozen campaign base `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99`. Authoritative peer review is `assembly-v2/review.yaml` (SHA256 `31cac38cae0cfb3dcfae4453a01402dc98d249f70ad9a7698a89b25eed5eae11`) in the sealed W04 independent W02 packet, whose 2,399-member SHA256SUMS is `99306617655b1e3df84368079e49f4341a0fd05667bdf9fedf18dda24f4f7ca7`. The coordinator verified all manifest members, rebound all188 case decisions and106 selected payloads, and independently repeated all106 native guarded writes and baseline/overlay partonomy. Structural validation passes; the scientific verdict remains needs_curation. These are unapplied proposal corrections, not changes already made to main or whole-owner/export approval.

`W02-F-INHERITED-PROPERTIES` (`W02C-006`, `w02-external-b-012`) concerns existing baseline fields, not newly introduced source aliases. Exact targets:

| Owner / frozen SHA256 | Contradiction |
|---|---|
| `L-Malic_Acid_Disodium_Salt_Monohydrate.yaml` / `4896efa3f3c06d572e3bf8dffffb131ab36f1e1a31fac75394acca8db7c43080` | Identity cas:207511-06-6 states L-disodium monohydrate, but formula C4H4NaO5−, PubChem197014 and stored structure carry one sodium, no water and unspecified stereochemistry. |
| `Coso4_X_7_H2o.yaml` / `3e14e4d57dab11eb3974f45db2894b12bd71aa7a761d823ae8ce401300ceba8d` | CHEBI:91244/formula/CAS state heptahydrate; InChI and SMILES describe anhydrous cobalt sulfate and are attributed to CHEBI53470. |
| `Voso4_X_N_H2o.yaml` / `bd15f57d4e547908edcffa874470f4cc2adfe672002fe3532be67c30e63caeaf` | Variable-n hydrate formula coexists with one-water InChI/SMILES copied from CHEBI87020 metadata. The ontology's same internal inconsistency is not independent evidence fixing n=1. |

Independently verify a form-specific property source, replacing only demonstrably exact supported fields; otherwise withdraw unsupported structure/CID/formula fields with preserved historical provenance. No generated structure, inferred fixed water count, stereochemistry or CAS reassignment is authorized. Retain valid identity/form evidence and record-level holds.

The complete baseline fields are preserved in W02C-006. Captured [CHEBI91244](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:91244) SHA256 `c8bf30f1c2b4e9c2bcc10bd256b68a090795c083c207baf2d9d9ebb201d0d3c5`; [CHEBI87020](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:87020) `fbf850a3ccae6ed0e62d3e78d0da4bd252a51af85a59c3d70294801eef4adaeb`. Reinspect exact malate registry/form evidence before any replacement; the current contradictory atom count does not license choosing a new identity.

Deduplication: closed871's fourteen repaired owners are a different set;315/321 preserve historical identity corrections, and321's recent comment concerns nickel properties, not these three blocks.268 is the general derived-chemistry mechanism;1220 owns a separate pentahydrate vanadyl alias/source question. Fresh exact-owner and comment searches found no tracker documenting these three current field corrections. Link those histories without reopening their successful identity fixes.

Preserve published original payloads/reviews, capture timestamps, histories, rejected text and all precise source/form/role/release holds. Prepare immutable corrected proposals through existing guarded validation, record claim-specific changes, and obtain independent review of the exact successor. No corpus application, owner merge, gate/schema/test/producer change or approval transfer follows from this issue.

items.title: Complete deferred source-qualified curation in final unmatched review shards
items.body:
Final coordinator review of two published source-review shards found that several no-change outcomes defer already-authorized curation rather than identify a missing scientific fact. Worker04 head `0d2c73e5aee5adb88782537755472d9ca0c5c3cd`; worker08 head `7efd3f8b98f9e822431dcb510c2c242a2569cfc7`; both depend on #1158 at `e000d66`.

Concrete examples:

- Worker08 case `CM_NAME:b9a945a3356d0c885eea986a2f6223e78c8e7d7163ee95629061a640294cbbe8` (H2O deionized) correctly distinguishes deionization from distillation, but its remaining requirement is to perform native owner lookup and use or create the appropriately scoped owner. [DSMZ533](https://www.dsmz.de/microorganisms/medium/pdf/DSMZ_Medium533.pdf) explicitly identifies deionized water in both main and trace stock. No proposal or completed lookup disposition accompanies that deferred step.
- Worker08 case `CM_NAME:e69128522cfe555f63dd51d4a23ece86363290b3839180386b090f368b28d1cc` (glycine-NaOH buffer) preserves a source-defined concentration and pH, and correctly finds a receiving-medium volume transcription error. [JCM906](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=906) specifies the separately prepared buffer. The decision defers representing the stock without explaining which missing fact prevents a bounded preparation identity. It must not be equated to pure glycine or assigned invented titrant amounts.
- Worker04 case `CM_NAME:2f91fab8feab468a33e48d01e2f0a1363b9ad70816766c69a1e8d68c0ed6f8d5` describes the [NBRC15](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=15) treated, clarified V-8 preparation but defers representing it until later curation. Lack of a molecular mapping or extraction yield does not by itself establish that a source-qualified preparation cannot be represented with an honest partial assertion.

Related outcomes defer normality-qualified NaOH stocks, source-specific top layers, C9322 supplied-form review, and malted wheat meal because an exact molecular/ontology mapping or later complete-owner review is absent. These are leads for reassessment, not predetermined identity approvals. Genuine solvent, formulation, provenance or supplied-form uncertainties may remain after primary research.

Reassess the full no-change cohorts against MAPPING_SEMANTICS sections3/6 and add-media. Complete supported proposal work, or state the precise scientific fact still missing and the actual primary-source searches. Keep receiving-medium dose/unit repair separate from ingredient identity. Never invent concentrations, solvent, chemistry, product equivalence, component completeness, or exact ontology matches; preserve all native holds and old review bytes. Require separate skeptical review of successor evidence/payloads and ordinary commits/pushes on the existing worker branches. No maintained data or export approval is requested from workers.

This extends the same class of completeness problem seen in #1163 and #1193 to distinct final shards; those earlier findings remain preserved. Exact frozen decisions and capture hashes are retained in the coordinator's immutable `w04-w08-deferred-curation-v1/review-inputs.json` and will accompany the campaign evidence. This is a review-completeness finding, not a statement that every listed source must map.

items.title: Document the protonation clause in MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 (#319)
items.body:
§3 settles hydration, salt form, stereochemistry and locants — but says nothing about **protonation**. The words *anion, cation, protonation, charge, conjugate* appear nowhere in it, and a bare anion label forces that choice. The corpus answered it inconsistently: **30** such labels sit on charged `X(n-)` terms, **5** do not.

## Resolved with live ChEBI definitions

This was the blocker on #319 and it was real — the local `chebi.db` carries **no definitions**, so the distinction could not be made offline. Fetched live, all five hold-outs read identically:

> *"A dicarboxylic acid anion obtained by deprotonation of **at least one** of the carboxy groups of X acid."*

That is a **deliberately protonation-agnostic** class — it already spans the mono- and di-anion. So `Malate`, `Succinate`, `Azelaate`, `Glutarate` and `Oxalate` **correctly stay where they are**. The research lane's caution about `Succinate` was right and generalises to all five.

## It also vindicates the merged Aspartate change

`CHEBI:132943 aspartate` carries **no definition at all**, even live — so nothing asserts it is deliberately agnostic. It is merely unspecified, and the sibling precedent (`Glutamate` → `CHEBI:29987 glutamate(2-)`) decides it. The descent applied in #331 stands, now on a positive test rather than precedent-plus-pH.

## The rule

> Read the parent's definition. **"At least one"** → stay. No definition, and `X(n-)` children exist → descend to the species present at growth-medium pH.

Written into §3 with a worked table covering both outcomes, the `Ascorbate` and `Protocatechuate` cases where there is nothing to descend to, the explicit caveat that the test **requires the live entry**, and the salt-parent convention from #322 (the narrowMatch parent follows the label, sidestepping acid-vs-anion).

**No data changes** — the five were already correct. This closes the last open question in the set.

pytest 880 passed (1 pre-existing, #311) · reconcile_sssom in sync · qc clean.

items.title: The bare-anion grounding convention is undocumented; curators are inferring it from practice
items.body:
## Finding

MIM applies a real, load-bearing convention when grounding bare anion labels:

> Ground a bare anion label (`Fumarate`, `Citrate`, `Lactate`) to the
> fully-deprotonated CHEBI class **where one exists**; otherwise to the
> bare-name class.

**It is written down nowhere.** A search across all `*.md` and `*.yaml` outside
`data/` for `bare anion` / `bare-name` / `fully deprotonated` returns one
unrelated hit in a 2026 batch-suggestions note. The convention exists only in
per-record `evidence.notes` on the records that already applied it, and in issue
#213 discussion.

A curator working the residual reconstructed it by reading 12 sibling records
and generalising — correctly, as it happens, but that is inference from
observed practice, not a documented rule. The next one may generalise it wrong.

## Why it matters more than a typical doc gap

The rule has a **per-record branch that is easy to miss**, and both sides of it
are currently live in the data:

- `Aspartate` → should be `CHEBI:29995 aspartate(2-)`; it is currently on
  `CHEBI:132943 aspartate`, a structure-free, definition-free class. The
  structural analogue `Glutamate` is already on `CHEBI:29987 glutamate(2-)`, so
  the data is internally inconsistent. 431 occurrences — the highest-traffic
  record found in the lane so far.
- `Ascorbate` → the bare-name class **is** correct here, because no
  `ascorbate(1-)`/`(2-)` term exists in ChEBI (verified: `CHEBI:22651`'s only
  child is `L-ascorbate`). Rewriting it to an `X(n-)` term would be wrong.

So a mass-application of "always use the deprotonated form" would fix Aspartate
and break Ascorbate, Succinate and Malate. The "where one exists" clause is the
whole rule, and it is exactly the part an undocumented convention loses.

A second consequence: `ols-label-exact-chebi` ranks **primary labels only**,
which is why `Aspartate` landed on the class in the first place — the matcher
cannot implement a convention nobody wrote down.

## Suggested action

Document it in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` alongside the predicate semantics, with:

- the rule and its `where one exists` branch,
- how to test the branch (search ChEBI for `<label>(n-)`; check the bare-name
  class for structure/definition — a structure-free class is a signal, not a
  target),
- the worked examples on both sides (Aspartate vs Ascorbate),
- and the note that structure-free classes must **not** be chemistry-enriched
  (an enrichment pass copying `L-ascorbate`'s structure onto the `ascorbate`
  class would be a #316-style defect).

Related: #213, #312, #315, #316, #317.

items.title: Apply 11 Edison-researched groundings from the microbedecoder residual
items.body:
Deep research (Edison Scientific / PaperQA3 `LITERATURE`) over the 142-record microbedecoder UNMAPPED residual that #201 and #202 deferred.

**141 records across 6 shards in 3h16m**, zero errors or rate limiting, every one with a complete provenance bundle under `research/ingredients/` (report, response JSON, citations, agent state, meta). Median **20 citations per report**.

> The runner is strictly serial — a plain `for` loop, no threading — so an unsharded run would have been ~12 hours, not the "few hours" previously assumed. Sharded via `--start/--limit`; per-slug output paths mean shards never collide.

## The yield is deliberately small

| outcome | n |
|---|---|
| enriched, correctly **still UNMAPPED** | 109 |
| **promoted** | 6 |
| **merged** into an existing record | 5 |
| no structured block — needs a curator to read | 20 |
| held back for curation decisions | 2 |

For much of this residual, *"source-backed evidence that no single ontology term applies"* **is** the result. The canary said so (it correctly refused to assert `(2)-D-lactose` = lactose) and the full batch agrees.

## Promoted (6) — target term held by no existing record

| record | → | quality |
|---|---|---|
| Bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate | CHEBI:17747 | synonym |
| Cis-aconitate | CHEBI:16383 | synonym |
| D-arabitol | CHEBI:18333 | synonym |
| Ferrous Ion | CHEBI:29033 | synonym — companion to `Ferric Iron → CHEBI:29034` from #202 |
| L-malate | CHEBI:15589 | synonym |
| Tetrathionate | CHEBI:15226 | synonym |

## Merged (5) — the term is already held, so a promotion would duplicate it

`3-hydroxy 2-butanone`→CHEBI:15688 (Acetoin), `D-lactate`→CHEBI:16004 ((R)-lactate), `Iso-butanol`→CHEBI:46645 (Isobutyl alcohol), `N-acetyl-neuraminic Acid`→CHEBI:17012, `Trimethyleneglycol`→CHEBI:16109 (1,3-Propanediol).

**7 of the 13 CHEBI recommendations pointed at an already-held term.** Applying those as promotions would have created exactly the defect #224 gates, and `just qc-duplicate-ids` would have failed the build — an unplanned check on that gate one day after it landed.

Every recommendation was **re-verified against the local `chebi.db`** rather than trusted: 2 exact label matches, 11 synonym matches, none without lexical support.

## Held back (2) — these are re-assignments, not merges

- `Beta-phenylethylamine` → CHEBI:18397, held by **"Phenethylamine Hydrochloride"**
- `Sodium L-glutamate` → CHEBI:64243, held by **"Sodium glutamate monohydrate"**

In both cases the existing holder is the **salt/hydrate mapped to the anhydrous free form as `EXACT_MATCH`**, CHEBI has no term for the salt or the hydrate, and the *incoming* label is the better match for that id. Fixing them means deciding what the current holder becomes — a curation call, filed separately rather than guessed at here.

`D-glucosaminic Acid` came back with a **KEGG** id, which is not a MIM identifier scheme; it needs a CHEBI equivalent or a minted `kgmicrobe.compound`.

## New tooling

`scripts/merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` generalises the one-off merge logic from #214 — the second time it was needed. RAW_TEXT synonym onto the target, the source's upstream source_id (`kgmicrobe.trait:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:`) carried into the target's audit trail (#220), source record removed, **no SSSOM row** (the target already has one; SSSOM subjects are never synonyms). Dry-run first, refuses partial batches. Merging two *MAPPED* records remains the harder open problem (#226).

## Gates

`mapped_count` 2287 → **2293**; unmapped 581 → 570 records, UNMAPPED 526 → **515**; SSSOM **+6** rows.

`just qc` exits 0 — reconcile GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0, validate-strict 0 errors / 2884 files, round-trip 0 data differences, **qc-duplicate-ids clean**.

Note: `research/` and `reports/` are gitignored, so the 142 provenance bundles and the triage TSV are local-only and are not in this diff.

Related: #201, #202, #213, #218, #224, #226.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Review

Reviewed adversarially. **The chemistry was confirmed correct on all 11** — every CURIE resolves, none obsolete, every stored `ontology_label` byte-identical to ChEBI's, and charged-species grounding matches established convention (`Trithionate → trithionate(2-)`, `Sodium(+)`, `Calcium(2+)` are already on main). Counts, the 6 SSSOM rows' structure and sort position, and the folded-name collision count (17 → 16, one *resolved*) all verified independently.

Fixed here:
- **`Bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate` was filed `EXACT_MATCH` on a false premise.** ChEBI's label is `bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate` — spaced and lowercase — so the raw text is a *related synonym*, exactly like `Cis-aconitate` and `Tetrathionate` which were filed `SYNONYM_MATCH`. `--quality` is operator-supplied, not derived, so nothing caught it and the SSSOM row carried 0.99 against 0.95 for chemically equal-strength rows. Re-run; all six are now 0.95.
- **The merge script's source lookup was the very last-wins pattern its docstring claimed to refuse** — the #214 peptone hazard. Now strict, like the target's. Latent, not live (0 duplicate preferred_terms today).
- **The merge silently discarded source fields a synonym cannot represent.** Nothing was lost in this batch (all five sources were empty on every one), but the script is the reusable generalisation — it now refuses and names the fields.
- **Short TSV rows wrote the literal string `None` into the audit trail**, or raised `AttributeError` mid-loop.
- Corrected the file count (2884, not 2894) and the `kgmicrobe.trait` vs `kgmicrobe.compound` claim.

Filed rather than fixed: **#229** (a merged raw label vanishes from every flat export and from SSSOM — `D-lactate` used to resolve to `UNMAPPED_0654`, now resolves to nothing; affects #214's 9 merges too, and no gate sees it) and **#230** (`Arabitol` → `CHEBI:18403 L-arabinitol` asserts a stereochemistry the label doesn't carry; pre-existing, and fixing it is a two-MAPPED-record merge, #226).

Also filed from this batch: **#228** (two salt/hydrate records mapped to the anhydrous free form, which is why 2 groundings were held back).
